explanation: The constitution of 2 April 1976 writes autonomy for the Atlantic archipelagos into the state. The Azores and Madeira are autonomous regions with statutes of their own, a legislative assembly their voters elect and a regional government answering to it. Nothing of the kind had existed under the Estado Novo, which ran the islands as districts. The assembly elected on 27 June is that clause taking form eleven weeks after the constitution came into force. The ballot fell on the same day as the presidential election, which is the state hurrying to fill the institutions it had just created.
